label: heart-s3
summary: The model is a near-linear logistic score for heart disease (training AUC 0.941). Most of its ranking comes from the direct edges: replacing them by their mean contributions drops training AUC to 0.470. The largest direct terms raise the score with the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (1.98 per sd), male sex (1.41), a flat ST slope (1.27) and having no chest pain (0.97). Five hidden units add corrections. For the typical patient, predicted risk rises with age up to 59 years (21%) and then falls (15% at 75 years) because an age hinge switches on. A blood-pressure hinge flattens the rise in risk with resting blood pressure, and switches on at a lower pressure when the ST segment is upsloping. Atypical angina raises the score through its own unit, by 1.00 on average for the 42 training patients with it. A minor unit lowers the score a little for non-anginal chest pain, and a flag is fitted to the 2 training rows with the rare thal code. Replacing the hidden units by their affine fits leaves training AUC at 0.938.
